metaData.title: How Claude Code Agent Is Designed and Implemented
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Claude Code source code leak, revealing its core architecture: AI decision-making logic accounts for only 1.6%, while the remaining 98.4% consists of deterministic engineering infrastructure such as permission control, context management, tool routing, and error recovery.
metaData.summary: Based on the Claude Code source code leak, the article deconstructs its overall architecture in depth. The author points out that the core of Claude Code is not a sophisticated AI reasoning mechanism, but an engineering project centered around AI. The article details the five core modules of the system: the entry layer (five operating modes), the Agent main loop (a seven-stage state machine), QueryEngine (an intelligent HTTP client), the tool system (plugin-based architecture with lazy loading), permission control (matrix management and refusal tracking), context compression (a five-level gradient strategy), and the Memory system (a three-layer pointer index architecture). The article emphasizes that the difficulty in building a reliable AI Agent lies not in calling the model, but in managing all the engineering infrastructure surrounding it.

mainPoints.point: Claude Code's AI decision logic accounts for only 1.6%; the rest is engineering infrastructure.
mainPoints.explanation: The source code leak reveals that the code actually calling the model is just a thin layer; what supports the product is a large amount of highly engineering-intensive scaffolding code, such as permission control, context management, and tool routing.

mainPoints.point: The Agent main loop is a seven-stage state machine driven by stop_reason.
mainPoints.explanation: The main loop controls the flow through three state values: end_turn, tool_use, and max_tokens, enabling a cyclic iteration of model autonomous decision-making, tool invocation, and context compression.

mainPoints.point: The tool system adopts a plugin-based architecture, optimizing token consumption through a lazy loading mechanism.
mainPoints.explanation: Over 40 built-in tools and MCP external tools unify their interfaces through an abstract base class. The defer_loading mechanism ensures that only 8-12 potentially useful tools are injected per round, saving approximately 96% of tokens.

mainPoints.point: Context compression employs a five-level gradient strategy, ranging from zero-cost truncation to high-cost full compression.
mainPoints.explanation: From Snip and MicroCompact to Full Compact, the system automatically selects the compression level based on the remaining token budget, ensuring stable operation for long tasks.

mainPoints.point: The Memory system adopts a three-layer pointer index architecture to avoid full knowledge occupying the context.
mainPoints.explanation: MEMORY.md only stores pointer indexes (approximately 2000 tokens), topic files are loaded on demand, and CLAUDE.md static configuration is persistent. This design is similar to the B+ Tree index concept in databases.

keyQuotes: Only 1.6% of it is actual AI decision logic; the remaining 98.4% is deterministic infrastructure—permission control, context management, tool routing, and error recovery logic.
The difficulty in building a reliable AI Agent lies not in calling the model, but in managing everything around the model.

What an AI Agent can do depends on the tool system. How well an AI Agent performs depends on context management. Whether an AI Agent runs stably in real tasks depends on permission control and error recovery.
Building a reliable AI Agent is essentially an engineering problem, not an AI problem.
Simplicity is deliberately pursued. The more complex the permission system, the higher the likelihood of vulnerabilities.
